GeometricSatakeAndFusion.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has perfectoid spaces, diamonds, v-sheaves, the Fargues-Fontaine curve, loop groups, affine or Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannians, Schubert cells, perverse sheaves, universal local acyclicity, hyperbolic localization or any six-operation formalism. 'Satake', 'Schubert', 'Perverse' and 'Fargues' have no hits in the declaration index or in either Lean tree. The libraries supply inputs, not targets. From Mathlib: Witt vectors, perfection, tilting and untilting, Fontaine's theta with the period rings B_dR^+ and B_dR over a p-adically complete ring, the module Grassmannian, abstract t-structures, derived categories and symmetric monoidal categories. From Tau Ceti: simply connected root data for every Dynkin type, a Chevalley involution of Geck's Lie algebra, and Tannakian reconstruction for a commutative Hopf algebra. Two things the roadmap treats as work are closer to done than it suggests. The pinned dual root datum exists as combinatorial data (TauCeti.DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum with RootPairing.flip). The double-coset Hecke ring the classical Satake comparison needs exists abstractly (Mathlib's HeckeRing, with Tau Ceti's ring structure), and Shimura's polynomial-ring theorem is proved for GL_2. Everything geometric is genuinely missing: the loop-group and Schubert geometry of GS0; the Bhatt-Scholze projectivity route (neither library has ample, nef or semiample line bundles); the relative perverse t-structure of GS1; convolution and fusion; and the Tannakian identification with the pinned dual group.

HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. The objects it constructs - Hecke stacks of modifications of G-bundles on the Fargues-Fontaine curve, local shtuka moduli, their J_b(E) and Weil actions, and the Hecke functors T_V built from Satake sheaves - have no counterpart in either library: 'shtuka' and 'Satake' have zero hits in the declaration index and in both Lean trees, and there is no v-stack, diamond or six-operation formalism to state any of them in. The libraries supply only ambient algebra: Mathlib's condensed sets and modules with the free/forgetful adjunction (the coefficient formalism HS1's continuous action needs), its rigid monoidal categories with exact pairings (the abstract shape of HS4's creation/annihilation identities), its adic completion, and its abstract double-coset Hecke ring; Tau Ceti's profinite and pro-p group theory is the group-theoretic side of HS3's pro-p level subgroups. Everything the roadmap actually states is genuinely missing, and its whole upstream chain (RelativeFarguesFontaine, BunGAndNewtonStrata, GeometricSatakeAndFusion, VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories) is missing with it. The nearest existing work in the atlas is the function-field mirror in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1-GS.4, which is itself unbuilt.

LanglandsParameterStacks.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. The central objects are all absent: the Weil group of a local field, nonabelian continuous cocycles valued in a dual group, the cocycle scheme Z^1(W_E/P, Ghat) and its quotient stack, the excursion algebra, the coarse invariant quotient, and Perf of the parameter stack. Neither library has a Weil group, an L-group or dual group scheme (the dual root datum exists as RootPairing.flip), a quotient stack, geometric invariant theory, derived algebraic geometry or perfect complexes. The libraries do supply ambient theory the roadmap will build on. Mathlib has group cohomology and its continuous version for topological groups, extended in Tau Ceti with inflation-restriction, corestriction, Shapiro and long exact sequences, all with abelian coefficients (even Mathlib's multiplicative cocycles need a commutative coefficient group). Mathlib also has decomposition and inertia subgroups of a valuation subring (higher ramification groups are an explicit TODO, so wild inertia is not there), free and presented groups, flatness, regular sequences and the naive cotangent complex, invariant subrings, and the Stacks 0BR8 homeomorphism criterion behind universal-homeomorphism statements. Tau Ceti has the absolute Galois group with its Krull topology. Two targets the roadmap treats as a matter of specialization are further away than they look. LP3's Weyl and dual-Weyl modules with good filtrations are neither Tau Ceti's char-zero Lie-algebra highest-weight theory nor its GL_n Schur-Weyl `weylModule`. LP1's local complete intersection structure has no named predicate in Mathlib and can be stated only through regular sequences.

targets.note: Mathlib has the decomposition and inertia subgroups of a valuation subring, with the explicit TODO 'Define higher ramification groups in lower numbering', so wild inertia is not there; Tau Ceti has the absolute Galois group with its Krull topology and ramification groups for places of a function field, but nothing for local fields. grep -i for WeilGroup and for 'wild inertia'/'tamely ramified' over both Lean trees returns nothing: there is no Weil group anywhere.

All of it is abelian-coefficient. Nonabelian 1-cocycles Z^1(W, Ghat) with twisted conjugation, which is what a parameter is, are absent: grep -i for nonabelian/twistedConjug in declarations.tsv finds nothing relevant.

VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories.summary: Five of the six layers are unbuilt and one, VS2, is partly built. The condensed foundation VS2 asks to consume is genuinely in Mathlib and sorry-free: CondensedMod with its free/forgetful adjunction, Condensed.profiniteFree, Condensed.profiniteSolid as a pointwise right Kan extension, Condensed.profiniteSolidification and the CondensedMod.IsSolid predicate, together with exactness of limits and colimits in condensed modules. The layer's warning is also confirmed by the source: IsSolid's own docstring says it is not the correct definition for a general ring and prescribes the Z[X]-restriction-of-scalars fix, and Mathlib still carries TODOs that no profinite free module is yet proved solid. Everything else is missing. There is no v-topology, perfectoid space, diamond or Artin v-stack in either library, no six operations and no exceptional functors, no universal local acyclicity, no hyperbolic localization, no Drinfeld lemma, no solid tensor product or internal Hom, no D_solid or D_lis, no smooth representations of locally pro-p groups, and no Bernstein-Zelevinsky or Verdier duality. What the libraries contribute beyond VS2 is ambient machinery the roadmap will build on rather than targets: Mathlib's sheaves on sites and its IsStack descent condition, pretriangulated categories and t-structures, group cohomology as derived invariants, formal smoothness, and Z_ell; Tau Ceti's pro-p group theory is the group-theoretic side of VS4's level subgroups.

targets.target: Artin v-stacks by representable diagonals and the cohomologically smooth atlas condition (FS IV.1); atlas independence and stability under fibre products
targets.note: Mathlib's IsStack is the descent condition on a pseudofunctor over a site; it is not an algebraic or v-stack, has no diagonal or atlas notion, and there is no v-topology, no perfectoid space and no diamond in either library.

targets.note: Absent; there is no enhanced (stable infinity-categorical) coefficient category in either library.

targets.note: Neither library has exceptional functors f^! or f_!; Mathlib's sheaf operations on a site are pushforward/pullback only.

targets.target: Partial compact-support functors pi-sharp of FS IV.5 for stacks outside the representable ECD class, with independence of presentation, adjunctions and base change
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions (FS IV.2)
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'universally locally acyclic' over both Lean trees returns nothing, and neither library has the etale cohomology of adic spaces in which it would be stated.

targets.target: Base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties of ULA with their compactness hypotheses
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3-IV.4 for relative section functors on Fargues-Fontaine curves; the tangent/cohomology calculation, positive-slope condition and resulting cohomological smoothness
targets.note: Mathlib has formal smoothness of algebras by the infinitesimal lifting criterion, and a Jacobian criterion for smooth ring maps, but the Jacobian criterion here is FS IV.4 for the Banach-Colmez section functor of a bundle on the Fargues-Fontaine curve, and that curve does not exist in either library.

targets.note: Absent from both trees.

targets.note: Absent; there is no partial Frobenius and no Weil group in either library.

targets.target: Mathlib's CondensedMod with its free/forgetful adjunction and its profinite free-module and solidification maps
targets.note: Present and sorry-free exactly as the layer describes. Condensed sets are sheaves on CompHaus for the coherent topology, CondensedMod R their module objects; free/forget is an adjunction, profiniteSolid is the pointwise right Kan extension of the free functor on finite sets along FintypeCat.toProfinite, and profiniteSolidification is the natural map R[S] -> R[S]^solid.

targets.note: Mathlib has AB-style exactness of limits and colimits in condensed modules and a monoidal structure on light condensed modules, but no solid tensor product, no internal Hom of solid modules and no universal property of solidification.

targets.note: Mathlib has pretriangulated categories with distinguished triangles, which is the ambient formalism, but no semiorthogonal decompositions and no Harder-Narasimhan stratification of a stack of bundles.

targets.note: Absent; compact induction of smooth representations does not exist in either library.

targets.note: Absent; grep -rn -i 'Bernstein' over both Lean trees returns nothing, and there is no Bun_G.

targets.note: The only occurrences of 'Verdier' in either library are the left/right Verdier localizing subcategory classes, which are about Verdier quotients of triangulated categories, not about the dualizing-complex duality D = RHom(-, omega); ULA objects are absent too.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CFSGStatement.summary: This roadmap is substantially built in Tau Ceti, and the whole CFSG directory is sorry-free. I0 is complete: PrimePower, LieTypeIndex with its validity and duplicate predicates, ValidLieTypeIndex, SuzukiReeIndex, GraphTwistedIndex, SporadicName with card_sporadicName = 26 proved by decide, CFSGIndex, the numbered data with rank defined as dynkinType.rank, the algebraic-closure Closure, and all six pinned permutations with their Cartan-matrix invariance. S0 and S1 are complete too: the Relator expression type with its compilation theorem, the GroupPresentation metadata record with the layer's exact fields and no checksum, and all twenty-six transcribed sporadic presentations with their count checks, including the Monster by the Y443 route with Ivanov's central relator appended, exactly as S1 prescribes. The Lie-type lane is built for thirteen of the seventeen constructors. Carriers, Steinberg maps, fixed points and candidate groups exist for A, 2A, B, C, D, 2D, E6, 2E6, E7, E8, F4, G2 and the Suzuki family, on the spin, symplectic, minuscule, Geck and standard-linear carriers the L0 table designates, and the root-datum Steinberg map is complete for every valid index. Genuinely missing: (1) the tripled D4 carrier, and hence the 3D4 branch. Triality, gamma3 o Frob_q and their pinned equations exist only on the Geck carrier, which the roadmap rules out for 3D4, though the generic numbered-symmetry automorphism of toral closures is built. (2) The short-root G2 and F4 carriers as group schemes with their special isogenies, and hence the Ree and Tits branches. The short-root modules exist only as Lie-algebra representations, and the G2 and F4 isogenies only on the root datum and the split torus. (3) The uniform ValidLieTypeIndex.Group. (4) L5 in its entirety, with the pinned Chevalley--Demazure group scheme over Z that L0's pinned route and L1's uniqueness theorem cite from the reductive-groups roadmap. Of that theorem only the uniqueness step, rigidity of toral Kostant carriers, is built. (5) A0's CFSGIndex.Group and ClassificationStatement. One A0 target the document treats as work is already done, more generally than stated: TauCeti.exists_mulEquiv_of_forall_finite_isSimpleGroup_zero is classificationStatement_of_zero for an arbitrary indexed family.

The 30 present targets and the citations behind the 38 partial ones were checked at source: the whole CFSG development was read declaration by declaration, with its variable lines and hypotheses. Every absent target in the four diamond roadmaps was searched again by concept, name and synonym in declarations.tsv and both source trees, with about 70 concept sweeps and every hit opened before use. Every citation (183 before, 199 after, 177 distinct) resolves in declarations.tsv at its file and line; none is private or deprecated after replacing Ring.Perfection, and no cited file has sorry or axiom outside comments. The audit's picture holds. CFSGStatement is substantially built (I0, S0 and S1 built; thirteen of seventeen Lie-type constructors carried through to candidate groups; A0's universe lowering proved in general). The geometric Satake, Hecke-stack, parameter-stack and v-stack roadmaps are unbuilt apart from VS2's Mathlib condensed foundation.
